tasks.title: Implement snapshot-bound code links and safe reference resolution
tasks.description:
Outcome: Resolvable code links with distinct historical location, current location and meaning review.

Current implementation: Descriptions currently contain text/file:line references; these drift after source changes and do not identify symbols across unrelated tasks.

Implementation responsibility:
- Define language-independent CodeLink, source anchor and resolution states using project/workspace/execution/configuration and recoverable baseline content.
- Resolve current targets through compatible available providers and structural/text evidence; preserve ambiguous, missing, unsupported and stale outcomes instead of guessing by name/line.
- Track rename/move/dirty edits and external changes without silently rewriting rationale or Accepted Decisions.
- Provide reverse code-to-task/decision lookup and exact historical views, using server-owned persistence and revision-safe navigation.
- Exercise the T002/T010/T020 function scenario: later work discovers prior signature changes, callers, slim/pure/functional constraints and missing intent.

Acceptance and evidence:
- File:line is dated navigation evidence only; stale or multiple candidates cannot silently attach to the wrong function.
- Historical location, current resolution and semantic review have independent states.
- Text-only and unsupported-language projects retain useful planning and explicit limits.

tasks.title: Capture large-task changesets and scoped code ownership
tasks.description:
Outcome: Automatic large-task changesets and honest attribution without per-function task proliferation.

Current implementation: Large tasks change many areas. Git diffs alone mix pre-existing dirty edits, concurrent work and changes produced by different executions.

Implementation responsibility:
- Capture execution baseline, checkpoints and closeout against the registered source workspace, including recoverable dirty content and configuration.
- Derive changed files/symbols/areas from available source evidence and preserve only observed attribution; overlapping or foreign changes stay uncertain.
- Link significant module/interface/function decisions and source tests to the changeset rather than requiring a written note for every modified function.
- Reuse T491 execution identity and T470 links for later discovery, deleted worktree recovery and cross-task impact. Do not auto-commit, reset or publish.

Acceptance and evidence:
- A large development task produces a queryable changeset with preserved initial dirty state.
- Later unrelated tasks discover earlier changes through common source targets.
- Concurrent/foreign changes are not assigned to the current task without evidence.

tasks.title: Version durable decisions and resolve their applicability to code
tasks.description:
Outcome: Durable scoped rationale and applicability across source revisions and task boundaries.

Current implementation: Single-owner Accepted Decisions already exist; missing source applicability and revision history can hide architectural constraints from later tasks.

Implementation responsibility:
- Version decisions and explicit supersession without duplicating owner records or erasing accepted history.
- Attach applicability to stable code areas/interfaces/anchors, requirements and source/configuration scope; retain constraints such as slim/pure/functional style.
- Resolve applicable rationale during context preparation and reverse lookup, distinguishing unknown intent from genuinely absent decisions.
- After relevant source changes, mark applicability for review; do not automatically rewrite approved intent or promote inferred text into decisions.

Acceptance and evidence:
- A later task retrieves applicable decisions even without an explicit task-to-task reference.
- New parameter/behavior changes preserve prior rationale and expose conflicts for discussion.
- Decision identity/ownership and accepted history survive rename/refactor.
